title: RNA Purification from Buccal Swabs, Nasopharyngeal Samples and Saliva using Monarch Total RNA Miniprep Kit
author: New England Biolabs
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.be93jh8n

steps.title: Stabilize Saliva Samples
steps.instruction: Immediately stabilize the saliva sample after collection.

substeps.instruction: Mix 200 µL of saliva sample with an equal volume of 2X Monarch DNA/RNA Protection Reagent.
If the reagent cannot be added immediately, place the sample on ice.

steps.title: Stabilize Swab or Transport Medium Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the sample by adding the protection reagent based on the sample type.

substeps.instruction: For swabs: Place the swab into a tube containing 300 µL of 1X Monarch DNA/RNA Protection Reagent and vigorously swirl to resuspend material.
For transport medium: Add an equal volume (up to 200 µL) of 2X Monarch DNA/RNA Protection Reagent to an aliquot of transport medium and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Sample Disruption and Homogenization
steps.instruction: Digest proteins and lyse the samples.

substeps.instruction: Add Monarch Proteinase K: Use 20 µL for every 400 µL of DNA/RNA Protection Reagent/Sample mixture, or 15 µL for every 300 µL of mixture.
Vortex briefly and incubate at room temperature for 30 minutes.
For swab samples: Vortex briefly and spin at 16,000 x g for 2 minutes to pellet debris, then transfer the supernatant to an RNase-free microfuge tube.
Add an equal volume of Monarch RNA Lysis Buffer and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Remove Genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Remove gDNA using the gDNA Removal Column.

substeps.instruction: Transfer up to 800 µL of the processed sample to a light blue gDNA Removal Column fitted with a labeled collection tube.
Centrifuge at 16,000 x g for 30 seconds.
Save the flow-through (containing the RNA) and discard the column.

steps.title: Bind RNA to Purification Column
steps.instruction: Prepare the RNA for binding to the purification matrix.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of ethanol (≥ 95%) to the flow-through and mix thoroughly by pipetting. (Note: To exclude RNA ≤ 200 nt, add only 1/2 volume of ethanol).
Transfer the mixture to a dark blue RNA Purification Column fitted with a collection tube.
Spin at 16,000 x g for 30 seconds and discard the flow-through.

steps.title: On-Column DNase I Treatment
steps.instruction: Perform optional on-column digestion of remaining gDNA.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL RNA Wash Buffer, spin for 30 seconds at 16,000 x g, and discard flow-through (or use vacuum manifold).
Combine 5 µL DNase I with 75 µL DNase I Reaction Buffer in an RNase-free tube and pipette the mixture directly onto the column matrix.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Wash RNA Column
steps.instruction: Wash the bound RNA to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL RNA Priming Buffer, spin for 30 seconds at 16,000 x g, and discard flow-through (or use vacuum manifold).
Add 500 µL RNA Wash Buffer, spin for 30 seconds at 16,000 x g, and discard flow-through (or use vacuum manifold).
Add another 500 µL RNA Wash Buffer and spin for 2 minutes at 16,000 x g.

steps.title: Elute RNA
steps.instruction: Recover the purified RNA from the column.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the column to an RNase-free microfuge tube, ensuring the tip does not touch the flow-through (re-spin for 1 minute if necessary to remove ethanol).

Add 30 µL to 100 µL of Nuclease-free Water directly to the center of the matrix and spin for 30 seconds at 16,000 x g. (Note: ≥ 50 µL is recommended for best results; 30 µL gives > 80% recovery, 100 µL gives maximum recovery).
If performing spectrophotometric analysis, re-spin and pipette from the top of the liquid to avoid silica particle interference with A 260/230.

steps.title: Store RNA
steps.instruction: Store the eluted RNA according to the required duration.

substeps.instruction: Place RNA on ice for immediate downstream use.
Store at -20 °C for short-term storage (less than one week).
Store at -80 °C for long-term storage.
Optional: Add EDTA to a final concentration of 0.1–1.0 mM to reduce contaminating RNase activity.
